title: Local dimensions and cotangent spaces of sufficiently close finite-type models
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Present $\widehat A$ as a filtered colimit of finite-type $A$-algebras $B_\alpha$, with maps $s_\alpha:B_\alpha\to\widehat A$. Fix finitely many finite-type $\widehat S$-schemes $Z_j$, and models $Z_{j,\alpha}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}B_\alpha$ at sufficiently large indices [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist $\alpha_0$ and $n_0\geq2$ such that for every $\alpha\geq\alpha_0$, $n\geq n_0$, and $A$-algebra map $u:B_\alpha\to A$ with $u\equiv s_\alpha\pmod{\mathfrak m^n\widehat A}$, the pullback $Z_{j,u}$ has the same closed fibre as $Z_j$ and, at every point $z$ of this fibre, $$\dim\mathcal O_{Z_j,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z_{j,u},z}.$$ Moreover their restrictions to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^2)$ identify by the given coefficient congruence, and this identifies their residue fields and cotangent spaces $\mathfrak m_z/\mathfrak m_z^2$ compatibly with every specified model function. If $Z_j$ is regular at $z$, then $Z_{j,u}$ is regular at $z$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-weil-residue-field]. All assertions can be imposed simultaneously on a specified finite diagram, including finitely many closed subschemes and their intersections [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. The same assertions hold for models over strict localizations of the $B_\alpha$ at a compatible point over the closed point of $S$, using local sections with the same congruence [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].

source.place: III Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.4(i)–(iii), printed pp.41–43, with the finite-diagram convention of III §2 and the marked applications in the proof of III 6.2, printed pp.44–45; XV 3.3.2, printed p.224. The strict-local variant is obtained by representing the finite data on pointed etale neighborhoods before applying the finite-type assertion.
